name: Sanctions & coercion
summary: EU prepares a 22nd Russia sanctions package aimed at banks, crypto and third-country loopholes; no payment cut-off found
state: On 12 Nov Commission President von der Leyen said the 22nd package against Russia would be presented before the 26–27 Nov special European Council, and EU diplomats said it would add restrictions on banks, crypto platforms and routes through third countries (TimesLIVE, 12 Nov). On 16 Nov Kaja Kallas said the package would be presented within days (UNN). Searches on 28 Nov found no confirmed adoption, no major economy cut off from payment systems and no large-scale seizure of sovereign assets, so Watch holds.
for_you: Firms trading with Russia or through third-country intermediaries face more compliance checks as packages widen. The UK's OFSI and the EU publish the official lists of designated people and entities.
rubric_hit: Watch: major new sanctions package (EU 22nd Russia package in preparation); no payment-system cut-off or sovereign asset seizure

sources.title: TimesLIVE — EU to unveil new Russia sanctions package by year-end
UNN — The EU will present its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia in the coming days: Kallas

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
drivers: Russia/Iran sanctions packages, secondary sanctions, frozen-asset decisions, export controls.
